cosa.definition: The primary algebraic unknown ('the Thing') in the Regola dela Cosa (Arte Maggiore, Summa Part I, Dist. VIII), printed with the syncopated abbreviation .co. and corresponding geometrically to the side of a square.

censo.definition: The second Cossic power, equal to cosa multiplied by itself (x^2), abbreviated .ce. from the Latin census translating Arabic māl ('wealth' or 'square estate').

cubo.definition: The third Cossic power (x^3), abbreviated .cu.; on fol. 150r Pacioli famously noted that general equations mixing cubo, censo, cosa, and numero had not yet yielded to a universal rule.

censo-de-censo.definition: The fourth Cossic power ((x^2)^2 = x^4); Pacioli shows on fol. 149v–150r that biquadratic trinomials in .ce.ce., .ce., and numero reduce directly to the three compound quadratic canons.

piu-e-meno.definition: Syncopated operational signs standardized in print across Summa Dist. VIII for additive (.p̄.) and subtractive (.m̄.) terms, accompanied by the four sign laws of multiplication ('meno via meno fa più').

radice-universale.definition: Pacioli's prefix radical operator .℞.u. governing an entire binomial or polynomial radicand (playing the grouping role of the later vinculum over √(...)).

binomio.definition: An additive compound irrational a + √b or √a + √b classified into six species following Euclid Book X, Definitions II.1–6 and Propositions X.36–X.72.

residuo.definition: A subtractive compound irrational such as √125 − 5 or 15 − √125 (the two segments of 10 divided in extreme and mean ratio), classified into six species following Euclid X.73.

capitoli-composti.definition: The three positive-coefficient three-term quadratic forms on fol. 145r: (1) censo + cose = numero, (2) censo + numero = cose, and (3) cose + numero = censo, proved geometrically on fol. 146r by Euclid II.4–II.6.

proportione.definition: In Renaissance Euclidean terminology (fol. 68r–69v), the quantitative relation (habitudo) of one magnitude to another of the same kind—whereas a relation of ratios (a:b = c:d) is called proportionalità.

proportionalita.definition: Equality or similitude of two or more ratios (e.g., continuous a:b = b:c or discontinuous a:b = c:d), governed by the six Euclidean modi arguendi on fol. 74r.

multiplex.definition: First Boethian genus of greater inequality in which the antecedent contains the consequent an exact integer number n >= 2 times (dupla 2:1, tripla 3:1, quadrupla 4:1).

superparticularis.definition: Second Boethian genus in which the greater term contains the lesser once plus a single aliquot part 1/n: sesquialtera (3:2, musical fifth), sesquitertia (4:3, musical fourth), sesquioctava (9:8, whole tone).

superpartiens.translation: Superpartient Genus ((n + r) : n, 1 < r < n)
superpartiens.definition: Third Boethian genus in which the greater term contains the lesser once plus r > 1 proper parts (e.g., 5:3 = superbipartiens tertias).

modi-arguendi.translation: Six Euclidean Transformational Modes of Proportion
modi-arguendi.definition: The six inference rules expounded on fol. 74r from Euclid Book V: conversa, permutata (alternando), congionta (componendo), disgiunta (dividendo), eversa (convertendo), and equa (ex aequali).

media-et-estrema-ragione.headword: proportione avente el mezzo e doi estremi
media-et-estrema-ragione.definition: Euclidean division of a magnitude AB at C so AB : AC = AC : CB (Euclid II.11, VI.def.3, VI.30, XIII.1), called 'Divina Proportione' in Pacioli's 1509 treatise.

numero-perfetto.definition: An integer equal to the sum of its proper aliquot divisors (6, 28, 496, 8128, ...), generated via Euclid IX.36 on Summa Part I, fol. 8r whenever the geometric sum 2^n - 1 is prime.

inventario.definition: Complete dated enumeration on a single day of all cash, jewels, merchandise, real estate, debtors, and creditors owned by a merchant (De computis Cap. 2–3, fols. 198v–199r).

memoriale.definition: First chronological book of the Venetian counting-house in which every transaction is written down immediately as it occurs by any clerk or factor in whatever local coinage was used (Cap. 5–6).

giornale.definition: Second principal ledger book converting Memoriale items into uniform money of account using the syntax 'Per <Debitore> // A <Creditore>' with marginal Quaderno folio fractions (Cap. 10–12, fol. 201r–201v).

quaderno.definition: Third principal book indexed by an alphabetical Repertorio (Alfabeto), placing Dare (debits) on the left verso and Avere (credits) on the facing right recto in four currency columns l. s. g. p. (Cap. 13–14).

per-a.definition: Canonical Venetian Giornale markers explained in Cap. 11 (fol. 201r): 'Per' designates the debtor account first, separated by two oblique strokes '//' from 'A', which designates the creditor account.

cassa.definition: Real ledger account tracking physical specie on hand; in Cap. 12 (fol. 201r) Pacioli states the domain invariant that Cassa must always be debtor or zero—never creditor.

cavedal.definition: Venetian orthography for capitale ('tutto il tuo monte corpo di facoltà presente', Cap. 12, fol. 201r), credited at opening against Inventario assets and credited/debited with net profit or loss from Pro e Danno at closing.

pro-e-danno.definition: Summary nominal account (Cap. 27) collecting merchandise gains on Avere and losses/expenses on Dare before transferring net income into Cavedal.

summa-summarum.definition: Grand total of all Dare postings and grand total of all Avere postings across the entire Quaderno (Cap. 34, 36); their exact equality confirms structural conservation before closing.

bilancio-del-libro.definition: Closing summary procedure (Cap. 34) transferring open asset, debtor, creditor, and Cavedal balances from an exhausted Quaderno A into a fresh Quaderno B (marked with the Sign of the Cross +).

ducato-di-conto.headword: lira di grossi a oro (l. s. g. p.)
ducato-di-conto.definition: Standard Venetian Quaderno accounting unit recorded on fol. 201v: 1 lira = 20 soldi = 10 gold ducats; 1 soldo = 12 grossi; 1 ducato = 24 grossi; 1 grosso = 32 piccoli (1 lira = 7,680 piccoli).

catetto.definition: Perpendicular dropped from a triangle vertex onto the opposite base; in Summa Part II, fol. 9v, dividing twice the Heron area (168) by base 14 yields catetto AD = 12.

possanza.definition: The area of the square on a segment (Euclidean dunamis / Wildberger quadrance): e.g., a sphere whose axis has possanza 48 (length √48) on Part II, fol. 70r.

botte.definition: Practical solid mensuration in Summa Part II, Dist. V modeling curved wine casks as frusta of cones or averaged cylinders from bung and head diameters.

balla.translation: Interrupted Ball or Crossbow Contest (Problem of Points)
balla.definition: Stake-division problem on Summa Part I, fol. 197r–197v asking how a pot of 10 ducats should be divided fairly when a race to 6 winning rounds is interrupted prematurely.
